title: Why Cris Pop built The Thunder Way around ordinary people who choose to act
summary: Cris Pop writes about visiting Dragoș Pătraru's Biblioteca Nației and why he wanted Pătraru as a voice at The Thunder Way's first event. The essay is mostly values-driven, but it holds a few usable founder lessons: build around ordinary people, recruit trusted voices when launching something that matters, and ask for the seemingly impossible.

principles.text: Build around ordinary people: what separates some is choice, not talent or luck.
principles.quote: none of us are born special or destined for greatness. What sets some apart is not talent or luck, but choice.

principles.text: When launching something that matters, recruit trusted voices that carry weight.
principles.quote: When you're building something that truly matters, you need voices that carry weight. Voices that matter in our society, the ones people trust, respect, and feel genuine.

principles.text: Ask for the seemingly impossible; it feels out of reach until you find the courage to ask.
principles.quote: something that seems impossible until you finally have the courage to ask.

principles.text: Invest in people and legacy rather than things you don't need.
principles.quote: He invests in people, in their education, in their growth, in building something that will outlast us all: a legacy rooted in community, knowledge, and care.

principles.text: Integrity means making tough choices daily and choosing what's right even when unpopular.
principles.quote: It means facing the issues most people avoid and choosing what's right, even when it’s not popular.

principles.text: Build what's missing instead of debating what's broken.
principles.quote: While others debate what's broken, he builds what's missing
